messages.subject: inla.make.lincombs question
parts:
Hello,

I have a model of the form:    Y = Covariate + X * b + Z * u     where the X * b + Z * u is a smoother.

I would like to calculate the smoother in INLA with the  inla.make.lincombs function. But I already get stuck with the X * b term.  The code below tries to calculate X[,1] * b[1] + X[,2] * b[2]    but it seems to add b[1] and b[2] for all N rows.

Any suggestions?

Thanks,

JB

#Simulate data:
N  <- 100
X  <- matrix(rnorm(N * 5), ncol = 5)
Z  <- matrix(rnorm(N * 15), ncol = 15)
Covariate <- rnorm(N)
beta  <- c(1, 2)
b <- rnorm(5)
u <- rnorm(15)
eta <- beta[1] + beta[2] * Covariate + X %*% b + Z %*% u
Y <- rnorm(N, mean = eta, sd = 0.5)

#INLA model:
u <- 1:N
f <- Y ~ 1 + Covariate + X + f(u, model = 'z', Z = Z, constr = TRUE) 

#Run inla:
Test <- data.frame(Y = Y, Covariate = Covariate)
lcs <- inla.make.lincombs(X1 = rep(1,N), X2 = rep(1,N))

Model1 <- inla(f,
               data = Test,
               lincomb = lcs,
                quantiles=c(0.025, 0.975))
summary(Model1)

data = Test,

r1= X[, 1] * Model1$summary.fixed["X1", "mean"] +

That is perfect...thanks. I don;t think I would ever have figured out that one.

Brings me to the next step.  I now have the linear part of the smoother...the X * b component. Now I need to add the Z * u part of the smoother. I know it is also given in the output of INLA...but not the sum of X * b and Z * u (which I will need for a CI).

Here is where I am:

i <- 1:N
f <- Y ~ 1 + Covariate + X + f(i, model = 'z', Z = Z, constr = TRUE) 

lcs1 <- inla.make.lincombs(X1 = cbind(X[,1]),
                          X2 = cbind(X[,2]),
                          X3 = cbind(X[,3]),
                          X4 = cbind(X[,4]),
                          X5 = cbind(X[,5]))

lcs2 <- inla.make.lincombs(i = diag(N), Z1 = cbind(Z[,1]))
#lcs <- c(lcs1, lcs2)
#names(lcs) <- c("lcs1", "lcs2")

lincomb = lcs1,
               quantiles=c(0.025, 0.975))



How do I add the  Z * u columns to the X * b part? I tried to follow the example in Section 5.4.5 in Blangiardo and Cameletti...but that crashes with the Z.

Any feedback is welcome!

JB

c(Z%*%u, u)

hence the first N elements is what you want.
